summary: Independent reconciliation candidate for the vehicle_physics scope built from eight validated source proposals (vehicle_physics_01, vehicle_physics_02a, vehicle_physics_02b, wave_001_vehicle_physics_01..05). The reconciled engine map keeps the packet's class groupings wherever common ownership of the per-vehicle 'this' base is unproven (rule 7) and merges only where independent proposals agree by name AND share direct call/ownership evidence: VehiclePhysicsBody (vehicle_physics_01:2 + wave_001_vehicle_physics_01:0, joined by the 0x004E4790->0x0043E230 call and the shared wheel-dynamics record family), TireModelData (vehicle_physics_02a:1 + wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:8, joined because TireModelDataInit 0x004F34E0 calls the two TireModel sub-initializers 0x004F2B50/0x004F31F0), and Vehicle (vehicle_physics_02a:0 + wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:0, both gated by the same 0x32BC physics-mode selector and owning the 248-byte per-wheel record family). VehiclePhysicsObject (wave_001_vehicle_physics_03:0), VehicleControlState (vehicle_physics_01:4), F1CVehicle (wave_001_vehicle_physics_02:10) and the collision/config/state classes remain separate canonical families at their source trust because the packet repeatedly flags their owners as UNKNOWN and common ownership as unproven. Cross-source contradictions (0x32BC mode-flag reuse, 0x4018/0x401C/0x4024 dual meaning, 0x3510/0x3514 mass vs anti-roll, 0xCC8/0xD0C tracked-point vs wing flags, 0x9C buffer vs spring pointer, strided wheel-record families, tire init markers) are recorded in conflicts rather than erased. No trust was promoted; every required function and class proposal ref is placed in the output.

engine_subsystems.name: VehiclePhysics
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics simulation: suspension-strut contact solving and swept collision detection, tire/grip force propagation with distance falloff, per-wheel spring/damper and tire-brush force models, weight distribution and contact-patch adjustment, velocity/angular-velocity integration and the RK2 physics timestep, mode-dispatched per-vehicle physics ticks, input smoothing and gear selection, collision-normal resolution and broadphase/filtered collision lists, wheel-surface spatial resolution, track-environment parameter initialization, steering/transform math, and the global dynamics-matrix identity initialization.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleStateAndLifecycle
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-vehicle runtime state and lifecycle: vehicle-list and deduplicated name-list construction from the global vehicle array, AI relative-speed and gear-shift control, per-car physics state construction, qualifying tire-usage event encoding, vehicle reset/clear/property-set, respawn/race-restart and full state reset/destructor paths, audio configuration loading, collision spark/damage feedback, and suspension physics snapshot copying.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleConfiguration
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Vehicle and tire configuration loading: line-by-line .SVM/.HDV parsing and section dispatch, default/override file validation, suspension-setup section parsing, per-wheel brake/suspension data loading, engine-section parsing and engine-map field registration, damage-model parsing, damping-direction validation, full tire-model session initialization, tire-model data construction with zero-init/physics-default sub-initializers, and the per-frame physics state-buffer clear used during construction and wheel-dynamics init.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Owns the vehicle suspension strut array and the per-frame suspension solver chain: per-strut contact solving (VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation), swept contact detection (SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection), and tire/grip force propagation with distance falloff (PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field samples from proposal:class:vehicle_physics_01:0 kept as boundary clues: this+0x130 strutCount (int), this+0x134 strutArrayBase (stride 316 bytes), this+0x148 maximumPropagatedForce (float). Not a complete layout. Strut-relative offsets (+24/+72/+112..+156/+268/+272) are source:raw prose only and are not carried as field evidence (see SuspensionStrutArrayLayout contract).

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleTireModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Session-level per-wheel tire physics initialization: per-wheel compliance matrices, tire brand and compound application, suspension compliance and attach-point geometry, session setup envelope, interpolated tire-curve table, wear/thermal session tables, and the session init sentinels (this+0x30=-2, this+0x34=3).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field samples from proposal:class:vehicle_physics_01:1 kept as boundary clues: this+0x30/0x34 init markers, this+0x70 hudDisableFlag, this+0x1458 tireBrandId, this+0x145C tireCompoundId, this+0x1CFC curveTableBuffer, this+0x1D08 curveTableEntryCount, this+0x1DB4 wearSeedValue. Offset space (0x30..0x1DB4) does not overlap TireModelData's (0x0..0x13CC) in a way that proves identity; kept separate per rule 7.

canonical_type_families.name: TireModelData
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle tire model configuration data constructed once (ABI lead Tire_Model_Data_Init, LEGACY): handle slots with 0/-1 sentinels, compound count 15, friction/camber/slip and per-compound coefficients, zero-initialized runtime accumulator runs, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs, and the config path loaded through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from global 0x005EA438. Also owns the two sub-initializers called by TireModelDataInit: tireModelZeroInit (0x004F31F0) and PhysicsDefaultsInitializer (0x004F2B50).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Merged on call evidence: TireModelDataInit (0x004F34E0) calls both sub-initializers, and the 02a unresolved note explicitly names those sub-calls as parts of TireModelDataInit. Primary layout from proposal:class:vehicle_physics_02a:1 (handle slots 0x0..0x3C, compound_count 0x3C, coefficients 0x13A8..0x13CC); the 04:8 GUESS sub-initializer samples (0x10/0x14 zeroed head, 0x90..0xA4 zeroed tail) are treated as sub-structure boundary clues, not a separate object layout.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsBody
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame physics timestep and wheel-dynamics state: decodes the packed input packet, dispatches mode-specific setup/vibration bodies, runs per-wheel suspension updates, owns the per-wheel wheel-dynamics records, resets wheel-dynamics state each frame (WheelStateReset), initializes mass/center-of-mass/suspension, copies suspension datasets into the physics engine, and drives the sub-stepped RK2 integration loop with collision damage/DNF detection and inertia-tensor transforms.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Merged on direct call + shared-record evidence: WheelStateReset 0x004E4790 calls WheelDynamicsInit 0x0043E230, and both proposals name the class VehiclePhysicsBody at DERIVED trust and touch the vehicle-mode fields (this+0x32BC/0x32C8) plus the stride-62 wheel-dynamics record family (this+0x35A0/0x35B0). Field samples from both sources kept as boundary clues (this+0x32BC wheelDynamicsInitFlag, this+0x32C8 vehicleMode, this+0x35A0 wheelDynamicsRecords stride 62 dwords, this+0x39F4 frameResetSentinel, this+0x60 time accumulator, this+0x68 timestep). 0x0043E230's 1124-byte strided wheel-struct blocks (wheel 0 at this+0x5D8) are a separate stride family whose identity with the 248-byte records is unproven (see conflicts).

canonical_type_families.name: WheelSpringDamperState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-wheel spring/damper force computation: builds the suspension axis frame, computes spring/damper forces from wheel velocity, clamps to the friction/grip circle and writes force components along the wheel local axes.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field samples from proposal:class:vehicle_physics_01:3 kept as boundary clues: suspension axis 0x38/0x3C/0x40, wheel velocity 0x18/0x1C/0x20, spring stiffness/force 0x48/0x4C, force-out 0xD8/0xDC/0xE0, contact position 0xC4/0xC8. Not a complete layout. The second argument a2 (contact-patch frame, 9 floats) has an inferred layout (see unresolved).

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleControlState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Vehicle control and steering state: maps raw controller input into steering/throttle/brake commands, applies steering damping and per-wheel steering geometry, runs collision avoidance and lap/position transitions, and distributes torque/brake to the wheels.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Kept separate from VehiclePhysicsBody and Vehicle per rule 7: the packet explicitly flags that common ownership of the this objects across VehicleControlState members (0x004441F0, 0x00442060) and VehiclePhysicsBody members is NOT proven (GUESS grouping on overlapping offset ranges). Field samples kept as boundary clues (steeringOutput 0x0, throttleOutput 0x8, brakeOutput 0x10, pitLimiterState 0x1D30, lapState 0x1EF0, torque split fields 0x1554..0x1564).

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsStateBuffer
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Small physics state buffer object cleared per-frame: zeroes dwords 0..38 of the 40-dword buffer and frees the heap buffer pointer at +0x9C through the free wrapper (0x00587BCF) when present, returning the previous pointer.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field sample from proposal:class:vehicle_physics_01:5: this+0x9C heapBufferPtr. Note this+0x9C is also SuspensionSetup's spring_array_ptr (wave_001_vehicle_physics_01:6); the two proposals share the offset and 0x00435410 calls 0x004358F0, so a shared object is possible but unproven (see conflicts).

canonical_type_families.name: Vehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle runtime physics and state object: per-frame wheel/suspension/tire force simulation (contact-patch adjustment, weight distribution, per-wheel suspension/tire state blocks of 248-byte stride, anti-roll-bar and drivetrain parameters, 13-point contact transform, force-model summation, wheel output publish), the pit-stop conditional wheel-force setter, per-frame transform integration hub (VehiclePhysicsTick mode dispatch), setup-vector propagation, climb/vibration adjustment, yaw-recovery state machine, dynamics state reset, lerped physics state propagation, and proximity evaluation. Physics-mode selector at +0x32BC gates all of these.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Merged on name agreement (both proposals are named Vehicle), the shared 0x32BC physics-mode gate, and the shared 248-byte per-wheel record family (02a:0 base 0x35AC wheel-force blocks at 0x3664/0x375C/0x3854/0x394C; 04:0 per-wheel data at 0x35B0, 62-dword stride). Core responsibilities are complementary. Source trusts differ (02a:0 DERIVED, 04:0 GUESS); the merged family is carried at DERIVED with the 04:0 GUESS grouping documented. Field samples kept as boundary clues from both sources; the 0x4018/0x401C/0x4024 interpretation clash between sources is recorded in conflicts.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsObject
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle physics and state object (15-function grouping over a shared this base): default-initialized contact/geometry and suspension/strut constant block, 74-float-stride wheel-state block, respawn/reset/collision-zone state, audio playback sub-slots, per-frame integration step configuration, 3x3 orientation matrix plus world position, camera/rendering snapshot block, rigid-body point transforms, and collision damage-feedback thresholds.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Kept separate from Vehicle despite heavy offset overlap (0x34B0..0x34DC orientation/world block, 0x32BC mode): the packet explicitly states common ownership across the 15 functions is inferred but NOT proven, and the wheel-state stride (74-float/296-byte at 0xD4) differs from Vehicle's 248-byte records. Field samples kept as boundary clues (wheel_state_block_base 0xD4, orientation matrix 0x34B0, world position 0x34D4, integration fields 0x3498..0x34AC, collision feedback 0x3D48..0x3EB8).

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: The per-vehicle object: carries the driver-info region (0x4620..0x48BC) cleared/reset on reinitialization, the live AI-driver slots, the recalculated property slot at +0x48AC, and the reset path that composes the physics sub-objects (calls VehiclePhysicsBody wheel-state reset and VehiclePhysicsObject full reset).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Kept separate from Vehicle/VehiclePhysicsObject: 0x004C6E80 calls 0x004E4790 (VehiclePhysicsBody) AND 0x004E09E0 (VehiclePhysicsObject), so F1CVehicle is a caller/composer, not provably the same allocation. Field samples kept as boundary clues (DriverName 0x4620, VehiclePath 0x4714, SaveFilePath 0x4794, slot markers 0x4898..0x48A8, PropertySlot 0x48AC, sentinels 0x48B4=-8388609 / 0x48BC=11).

state_machines.name: VehicleModeDispatch
states: mode 2 = full setup-data copy + 14 subsystem state machines
mode 3 = vibration path + 4 vibration state machines + 14 subsystem state machines
other modes = no mode-specific body; all paths converge on effect/audio flag derivation
transitions: this+0x32C8 is read each frame; values 2 and 3 dispatch distinct bodies, everything else skips the mode body
both mode bodies end in the common braking/effect/bit-flag derivation and effect-field update

states.name: Mode0_FullUpdate
states.description: Integrate wheel-space transform chain, update HUD elements 43/44, query body motion state, run per-wheel collision/suspension geometry, trigger vehicle sound on instance-id match.

states.name: Mode1_VelocityThreshold
states.description: Velocity-threshold variant: VelocityThresholdCheck then fall through into case 2's shared integration.

states.name: Mode2_SharedIntegration_Torque
states.description: Shared integration plus wheel-torque accumulation and per-wheel suspension-parameter/vibration updates.

states.name: Mode3_DelegateTimestep
states.description: Delegate to the physics time-step for the referenced vehicle via VehiclePhysicsTimeStep on the vehicle array at 0x5EC6D8.

transitions: this+0x32BC == 0 -> Mode0_FullUpdate
this+0x32BC == 1 -> Mode1_VelocityThreshold
this+0x32BC == 2 -> Mode2_SharedIntegration_Torque
this+0x32BC == 3 -> Mode3_DelegateTimestep (delegates to VehiclePhysicsBody 0x004C73F0)
other value -> Default_Unhandled

state_machines.name: VehicleStepModeGate
transitions: mode flag this+0x32BC == 0 -> one-time TireModelInit into dbl_7C7428 then step path
mode flag this+0x32BC in [1,3] -> step path (HDV parse, substep clamp, force solving)
mode flag this+0x32BC outside [0,3] -> early return without stepping

state_machines.name: VehicleYawRecovery
states: NonZero_Accumulating: state dword obj+0x4064 non-zero; accumulate frame time at this+0x4004; past 15.0 reset counters and, in session 7 with the audio flag set, fire the audio effect
Zero_RecoveryCheck: state dword zero; off-track guard then nearest-path and lateral-bound recovery decision
RecoveryTriggered: recovery fired; reset counters, set this+0x3D60 = 2, emit render/AI-tracking notifications in session 7
transitions: Entry -> NonZero_Accumulating when obj+0x4064 != 0 and this+0x32BC == 1 and state != 2
NonZero_Accumulating -> NonZero_Accumulating when accumulator at this+0x4004 > 15.0 (reset counters; audio in session 7)
Entry -> Zero_RecoveryCheck when obj+0x4064 == 0
Zero_RecoveryCheck -> RecoveryTriggered when accumulator exceeds flt_7D0A8C and off-track and lateral bound test fails

state_machines.name: GearShiftControl
transitions: Default -> BlockedByTimer when shift_timer(this+0x3A10) > 0 (flt_59E440 zero threshold)
Default -> ReverseRequest when driverStatus(this+0x4510) == 6
Default -> PitModeNeutral when carConditions(this+0x3D6C) == 2
Default -> UpshiftReady when engine_rpm(this+0x39A0) > shift_rpm_threshold(this+0x3A18) and traction > 0.8 and current_gear < max_gear
Default -> DownshiftTail via JUMPOUT(0x4F62E6) when current_gear(this+0x39FC) > 1

state_machines.name: SurfaceContactResolution
transitions: PrimaryQuery -> ContactAccepted when element+300 >= this+0x10 and nearest-neighbor hit (flag 1) found, storing hit pointer at element+276 and contact height at element+24
PrimaryQuery -> SecondaryPlaneTest when element+300 == 1 and element+276 still null
SecondaryPlaneTest -> ContactCleared when |signed plane distance| outside hit+0x84/+0x80 bounds (element+276 = 0, element+296 = -1)
SecondaryPlaneTest -> ContactAccepted when within bounds, copying element+296 from the hit chain

state_machines.name: GearSelection
transitions: Gear-input flag ladder at +0x1FBC..+0x20C4 selects reverse/gears 1..6 when the ladder enable byte at +0x2428 is nonzero; no flag leaves UNSELECTED (-2)
Neutral override at +0x20F0 == 0 and global byte_7D1370 == 1 force NEUTRAL (0) when the ladder is still UNSELECTED
Gear-output slots outside the ladder (0x20F0 != 0) force the highest gear value 7

state_machines.name: PitLimiterHudState
states: state 1 = pit limiter engaged (calls HUDElementConfig(41, 2, blend))
state 2 = pit limiter with weather-noise blend, cleared when throttle output this+0x8 < 0.8
transitions: state 0 -> 1 when pit flag dword_7CC368 set, this+0x1D34 != 0, this+0x1EF0 == 0 and vehicle state mode this+0xD0 != 2 (guard:6)
state 1 -> 2 when the pit flag clears
state 2 is cleared when throttle output drops below 0.8

state_machines.name: TireWearModeSwitch
states: wear mode 0 = wear disabled: NaN-boxed max double written to this+0x1DB8 and the four wheel wear blocks zeroed
wear modes 1..3 = wheel wear blocks scaled by flt_8ACF9C over 4 iterations
transitions: read global dword_7CEA5C: 0 selects disable, 1..3 select scaling
when session type dword_7C56A4 == 7, this+0x1DB4 is additionally divided by flt_8ACF9C

state_machines.name: CollisionFeedbackGating
transitions: this[0] == dword_7C54E8 and gate bytes clear -> primary (player) feedback path
identity differs and restricted-mode flag != 1 -> main body runs
identity differs and race phase not in {1,3} -> main body runs
identity differs, restricted-mode flag == 1 and race phase in {1,3} -> suppressed

interfaces.name: SpatialGridQueryService
interfaces.purpose: Spatial-grid contact lookup and collision-surface normal extraction used by the suspension contact solver and the collision normal solver.

interfaces.name: TireForceSolverService
interfaces.purpose: Per-strut tire, grip and lateral force computation used by the swept contact pass and the per-frame force-propagation pass.

interfaces.name: PackedPacketDecoder
interfaces.purpose: Decodes the packed per-frame input packet into orientation components, steering bitfields, per-wheel data, velocity short-vectors, floats and subsystem bits.

interfaces.name: MatrixTransformLibrary
interfaces.purpose: 3x3 matrix-vector transforms, rotation tensors, Euler-to-rotation and coordinate-frame conversions shared across steering, suspension and physics-step code.

interfaces.name: TireCompoundResolution
interfaces.purpose: Resolve the tire brand (TireBrandLookup on global table 0x008AD254 with the session compound id) and then the compound index into the two base pointers into the compound data used by wheel-force evaluation.

interfaces.name: SuspensionForceEvaluation
interfaces.purpose: Per-wheel suspension and tire force helper models: suspension force split, quadratic/cubic polynomial evaluators, tire force/torque computation, quadratic force model, linear vehicle parameter evaluation, and quadratic force/torque curve evaluation, whose outputs feed the force summation.

interfaces.name: TireBrushModelService
interfaces.purpose: Tire-brush force model: per-frame force/torque solving with a lock protocol (1 = acquire, 0 = release) and per-wheel contact/spring-damper helpers.

interfaces.name: ConfigTokenStreamParser
interfaces.purpose: Shared token-stream reading, line decoding, scalar parsing and CRT range/setting registration helpers used by all vehicle config parsers (damage, engine, per-wheel brake/suspension, damping validation, SVM/HDV).

interfaces.name: MemoryService
interfaces.purpose: Heap scratch allocation/free primitives, operator-new wrappers, float-to-int conversion and stack-buffer cleanup helpers used across physics, config and audio paths.

interfaces.name: GlobalVehicleArray
interfaces.purpose: Shared global vehicle array (dword_8AC390 count, dword_8AC394 base, stride 1060) consumed by the vehicle-list and name-list builders and by configuration validation to index vehicle entries.

interfaces.name: SpatialNearestNeighborQuery
interfaces.purpose: Spatial structure (dword_5EA2C0) backing wheel-surface contact resolution and physics-node propagation.

interfaces.name: PhysicsParseBuffer
interfaces.purpose: Global session parse buffer byte_7C56C0 used both as the target of SVM/HDV vehicle-file parsing and as the global setter buffer for wheel-dynamics parameter pushes.

interfaces.name: PhysicsNodePropagationService
interfaces.purpose: Physics-node propagation with distance falloff over the global node set.

interfaces.name: CollisionDamageFeedbackService
interfaces.purpose: Collision damage/spark event services: ring-buffer event encoding, state transitions, per-zone repair-service dispatch and steering-geometry deformation.

interfaces.name: LifecycleResetService
interfaces.purpose: Vehicle substructure lifecycle: multi-system state init/reset, array and dual-array destructors, timer clamp, scale propagation and audio sub-slot initialization.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionStrutArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The vehicle physics node exposes a suspension strut array at this+0x134 with stride 316 bytes and element count this+0x130. Per strut the solver writes contact state (penetration depths at +112/+116, gravity-compensated contact force at +120/+124/+128), force propagation results at +136/+140 and a candidate force slot at +144, reads the wheel position at +148/+152/+156 and travel scale at +24, and requires linked-node (+268) and contact-feature (+272) pointers to be non-null for contact processing. VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation / SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection / PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff all share this array and per-strut ABI.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsStateBufferClearContract
compatibility_contracts.description: PhysicsBufferClear zeroes dwords 0..38 of the 40-dword buffer on the this object, frees the pointer stored at +0x9C through the free wrapper (0x00587BCF) and nulls it, returning the previous pointer (or 0). Callers are ConstructorStub (004353F0), SuspensionSetupSectionReader (00435410) and WheelDynamicsInit (0043E230), so the buffer is reset during vehicle/tire construction and wheel-dynamics initialization.

compatibility_contracts.name: WheelDynamicsRecordArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The vehicle physics body owns four wheel-dynamics records at this+0x35A0 with stride 62 dwords. VehiclePhysicsTimeStep stores per-wheel force values at this+0x35BC + i*62 dwords (mode 2), while WheelStateReset re-initializes the records each frame, setting identity 1.0 at record-relative indices 22/23/39 and zeroing the leading accumulator entries, and the first-frame guard this+0x32BC drives WheelDynamicsInit(0x007C7428).

compatibility_contracts.name: PackedInputPacketFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame vehicle input arrives as a packed packet: the region at packet+8 encodes orientation components, a steering bitfield, per-wheel data, a velocity short-vector, floats and subsystem bits decoded by the helper family 0x004B2420..0x004B2AD0. Auxiliary words at packet+52/+56/+59 carry flags: packet+52 bit 0x80 -> byte this+0x1069, packet+56 bits 0x8000000/0x4000000/0x2000000 -> braking byte this+0x105D and effect bytes this+0x1065/0x1067, and packet+59 bit 1 -> byte this+0x4024.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleSessionInitMarkers
compatibility_contracts.description: TireModelFullInitialize ends a session by setting this+0x30 = -2 and this+0x34 = 3 with this+0x38/+0x3C zeroed. VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate reads this+0x30 for the position-change state machine, and VehiclePhysicsTimeStep branches on the vehicle mode this+0x32C8. A replacement must preserve these sentinel semantics across tire-model init, control-state updates and the physics timestep.

compatibility_contracts.name: PerWheelStateBlockLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Four per-wheel state blocks of 248-byte stride on the vehicle object (base 0x35AC). The wheel-force field sits at block-relative offset 0x24 (absolute 0x3664/0x375C/0x3854/0x394C): SetWheelForceParameters stores four per-wheel force parameters there, and the per-frame update initializes and reads the same block layout. A replacement must preserve the stride and the block-relative offsets.

compatibility_contracts.name: ContactPointOutputBuffer
compatibility_contracts.description: The 13-point contact-position output buffer at vehicle+0x3AB8 (stride 12 bytes) is computed each frame, copied into the 28-byte-stride wheel output array at +0x1078, and consumed by the vertex/particle buffer allocation; the bounding radius is tracked at +0x3B6C with +0x3B70 = +0x3B6C + 0.1. A replacement must produce all 13 points and publish them to +0x1078.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsModeGate
compatibility_contracts.description: The flag at vehicle+0x32BC gates two paths: non-zero enables the per-frame suspension body-offset override and the wheel-force field-storage path in SetWheelForceParameters; zero disables the override and routes the same four parameters to a direct rigid-body force/torque application using the dbl_7C7428 scalar as the inertia-tensor argument. A replacement must preserve this gate's effect on both consumers.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionWheelRecordReturnPointer
compatibility_contracts.description: UpdateSuspensionAndWheelPhysics returns a pointer advanced through four per-wheel 33-double records starting at session+5200 (plus the axis blocks at session+5336/+5864). The caller 0x004E45B0 (LargeConfigFunctionWithPhysicsConstants) uses the returned advanced pointer; a replacement must reproduce the pointer arithmetic.

compatibility_contracts.name: TireModelDataHandleConvention
compatibility_contracts.description: The tire model data object's header uses handle sentinels (primary field 0, other handle slots -1), a compound count of 15, and alternating sentinel/zero handle pairs. Its config path is passed through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from the global buffer 0x005EA438. A replacement must preserve the handle convention and the config-loading call.

compatibility_contracts.name: SvmHdvConfigFileFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: Line-based '='-delimited configuration files with named sections (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, Frontleft/Frontright/Rearleft/Rearright, Basic). Recognized header keywords include Setting/Notes/Downforce/Balance/Ride/Gearing/Custom/Symmetric. In non-server sessions a file with no recognized header is rejected as an illegal .SVM file. A replacement executable must preserve '=' delimiter handling, section dispatch, and the rejection path.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsMatrixRowIdentity
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x00578F76 must set exactly one row of the double-precision dynamics matrix to an identity row (diagonal element 1.0, all other stored elements of that row 0.0), selected by argument 0..33, and return the selector argument unchanged on every path.

compatibility_contracts.name: WheelSurfaceContactResolution
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame wheel contact pass must preserve the grip-scale formula 1.0 - (flt_8AFEE8 + flt_8AFEEC)*0.5 stored at this+0x170, the wheel array stride of 316 bytes with count at this+0x130 and base this+0x134, the two nearest-neighbor queries (flag 1 primary, flag 0 secondary signed-plane bound test) on dword_5EA2C0, and the phase-flag reset this+0x174 = -1 at exit.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsIntegrationGates
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame physics integration must early-out when the physics-override double at 0x005D6D70 equals 1.0 or the enable byte at 0x007CE254 is zero, must save and restore the FPU control word, and must preserve the RK2 midpoint sub-stepping (half-step wheel-data copies, accumulator this+0x60) over the timestep field this+0x68.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleFileValidation
compatibility_contracts.description: ValidateVehicleConfigurationFile returns 0 only when both the default and override SVM/HDV parses succeed; on success the parse buffer byte_7C56C0 is cleared, the cost-display mode backup dword_7C56C4 = dword_7D0450 is taken before parsing, and when the commit flag is set the override path is copied into the caller's this+0 / this+8 string slots via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc and sub_568B00.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Consumers of the global vehicle array (dword_8AC390 count, dword_8AC394 base, stride 1060) rely on the driver-name byte at entry+124 and the driver-file path at entry+188; a replacement must preserve those field offsets and the array stride.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionSetupSection
compatibility_contracts.description: SuspensionSetupSectionReader must keep the degree-to-radian conversion factor 0.0174532925199433 for orientation fields, the spring-array growth rule (capacity +3 slots of 100 bytes via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper with per-slot category init), and the spring classification enums sliding/normal/free-damping (0/1/2).

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionNormalOutputConvention
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement must write the normalized collision normal into the caller output vector a3 as { -(v8*v6), v8, -(v8*v7) } with v8 = 1/sqrt(v7*v7 + v6*v6 + 1.0) derived from the feature plane coefficients, and return the spatial-grid query result (feature pointer or NULL).

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleInputSmoothingOutputOrder
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement must emit the smoothed control outputs through output pointers in the order a3=steering, a4=throttle, a5=brake, a6=clutch, a7=handbrake, a8=gear, with throttle/brake/clutch/handbrake clamped to the [0,1] float range and the gear output in {-2..7} with the neutral override honoring global byte_7D1370.

compatibility_contracts.name: DriverInfoClearSentinels
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement clearing the vehicle driver-info region must zero the byte fields at 0x4620/0x4660/0x4678/0x46B8/0x46F8/0x4708/0x4714/0x4794, write -1 into dwords 0x4710/0x4898/0x489C/0x48A0/0x48A4/0x48A8, 0 into 0x48AC/0x48B8, -8388609 into 0x48B4 and 11 into 0x48BC.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionNodeFreePoolProtocol
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement reusing collision nodes must push drained nodes onto the global free pool through dword_8AB700 (head), dword_8AB704 (tail), dword_8AB708 (used when the pool is empty) and increment dword_8AB70C (count).

compatibility_contracts.name: VehiclePhysicsObjectLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement executable must preserve the vehicle physics-state layout: wheel-state block with 74-float (296-byte) stride based at this+0xD4, 3x3 orientation matrix at 0x34B0..0x34D0, world position at 0x34D4..0x34DC, integration fields at 0x3498..0x34AC, and the 0x3D48..0x3EB8 collision feedback threshold block.

compatibility_contracts.name: TireBrushModelLockProtocol
compatibility_contracts.description: Callers of the tire-brush solver must bracket work with TireBrushModelForceSolver(1) to acquire and TireBrushModelForceSolver(0) to release; the physics step and the collision wrapper both follow this protocol.

compatibility_contracts.name: IntegrationSubstepClamp
compatibility_contracts.description: The integration sub-step count stored at this+0x3498 must be clamped to [1,64]; step-size fields derive as 1.0/(40*v6) and 1.0/(8*(5*v6+5)) and this+0x34AC mirrors the global race-time double.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsGlobalStateBlocks
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame setup reads global physics state: dword_7C8A18 (physics base; +28 orientation, +100 world position), dword_7C7918 (per-corner camera copy source), dbl_7C7428 (shared tire-model buffer), dword_5EA2C0 (physics node set), and the rotating noise table dword_8AAE70/flt_8AAE74 for randomized delays and damage draws.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionForceFormula
compatibility_contracts.description: The temperature-scaled suspension force is computed as (temperature_term + 273.16) * input_factor * 0.002778858444950814 * scale + addend; a replacement must reproduce this arithmetic.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionFeedbackRingBuffer
compatibility_contracts.description: Collision spark/damage events are encoded into a 432-byte-strided ring buffer: dword_83EE60 counts live slots (cap 1023), dword_8AAE64 is the advancing slot base, ProgressBarEventEncode writes the slot header and direction bytes at slot+8..+14.

compatibility_contracts.name: PerVehiclePhysicsStateLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement executable must preserve the per-vehicle state object ('this' base) layout touched every frame: orientation matrix block +0x34B0..+0x34D0, wheel/setup vectors +0x34D4..+0x350C and +0x3534..+0x3548, world position/velocity +0x10..+0x54, body-motion state +0xFE4..+0xFF8, per-wheel data at +0x35B0 (four entries, 62-dword stride), climb/vibration +0x3994..+0x39C4, and the physics-mode selector at +0x32BC (dispatched by VehiclePhysicsTick and read by VehicleYawRecoveryStateMachine, VehicleDynamicsStateReset and VehicleClimbAdjust).

compatibility_contracts.name: SharedPhysicsBufferAndRegistry
compatibility_contracts.description: dbl_7C7428 is the shared suspension/body-motion physics object read and reset by VehicleClimbAdjust, VehicleDynamicsStateReset and VehiclePhysicsTick; dword_7C54F0[dword_7C54DC] selects the active vehicle whose instance id (obj+0x4894) gates the sound trigger; dword_7C8B44/0x7C8B48 are reset before the trigger.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleStateArrayStride
compatibility_contracts.description: Vehicle state array rooted at global 0x5EC6D8 is indexed by the vehicle index field (this+0x4) with a 18624-byte (0x48C0) stride during VehiclePhysicsTick case-3 delegation to VehiclePhysicsTimeStep.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionTypeGatedDiagnostics
compatibility_contracts.description: Debug warnings during configuration load are suppressed when session type dword_7C569C == 5 (server), and recovery/audio notifications require dword_7C56A4 == 7; these globals gate diagnostic and notification side effects and must keep their semantics.

compatibility_contracts.name: HudElement43_44Contract
compatibility_contracts.description: VehiclePhysicsTick emits HUDElementConfig(43/44,...) each handled frame driven by the flags this+0x4018 (element 43) and this+0x401C (element 44, scaled by dbl_7C7598*4 clamped to 1.0); a replacement must reproduce these HUD updates or accept missing HUD output.

compatibility_contracts.name: DampingGovernorSemantics
compatibility_contracts.description: After each handled physics mode, the damping governor recomputes this+0x105B from v75 = 0.94 - this+0x1030*0.9 against globals flt_8AFECC/8AFEE8/8AFEEC every 16 ticks (counter this+0x4020); external pokes to +0x105B do not persist because the field is recomputed.

compatibility_contracts.name: InverseCoordinateTransformResultBuffer
compatibility_contracts.description: computeInverse3x3CoordinateTransform (0x0056D020) writes the inverse-transform result into the workspace buffer at this+0x10 (elements this+0x28 through this+0x80) and returns a pointer into that buffer; callers at 0x00439210 and 0x0056D930 rely on the returned pointer.

compatibility_contracts.name: GlobalPhysicsSolverStateZeroInit
compatibility_contracts.description: PhysicsStateZeroInit (0x00579CCF) zero-initializes a contiguous global solver-state region beginning at 0x008D2120 and ending with the 272-byte block at 0x008D3870 (span ~0x1860 bytes), mixing direct double assignments with block clears through sub_58BB10; a replacement executable must preserve this global layout and the double alignment of the cleared blocks.

compatibility_contracts.name: Matrix3x3VectorMultiplySemantics
compatibility_contracts.description: Matrix3x3VectorMultiply (0x00435E00) transforms an input vector by a 3x3 matrix; computeInverse3x3CoordinateTransform calls it twice on the two workspace input vectors, so a replacement must provide the same 3x3 vector-transform semantics for the two input-vector slots (this+0x04, this+0x08).

conflicts.subject: Common ownership of the per-vehicle 'this' base across VehiclePhysicsBody / Vehicle / VehiclePhysicsObject / VehicleControlState / F1CVehicle
alternatives: a single shared per-vehicle object
five separate sub-objects with mutual calls
a composition where F1CVehicle owns the physics sub-objects
conflicts.resolution: This candidate keeps the packet's five groupings separate (rule 7). Overlapping field bases (0x32BC mode flag, 0x34B0..0x34D0 orientation, 0x35A0/0x35AC/0x35B0 wheel records) and pervasive mutual calls do not prove a single allocation, and the packet explicitly flags common ownership as unproven for each grouping. F1CVehicle's reset (0x004C6E80) calls into both VehiclePhysicsBody (0x004E4790) and VehiclePhysicsObject (0x004E09E0), which supports composition over identity. Reconcile upward only if a later candidate proves a single base.

conflicts.subject: this+0x32BC physics-mode flag reuse across four class families
alternatives: VehiclePhysicsBody wheelDynamicsInitFlag (read)
Vehicle physics-mode gate (non-zero enables override/wheel-force path)
VehiclePhysicsObject step-mode dispatch (0 init / 1..3 step / else early return)
Vehicle physics tick mode selector (0..3)
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased: all four consumers gate on the same offset. The interpretation clash is the strongest evidence FOR a single per-vehicle object, but identity is unproven; kept as separate families with this conflict noted for the cross-reconciliation step.

conflicts.subject: Dual interpretation of vehicle offsets 0x4018 / 0x401C and 0x4024 across sources
alternatives: vehicle_physics_02a:0: 0x4018 post_update_reset_byte, 0x401C post_update_reset_b, 0x4024 spring_rate_accumulator
wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:0: 0x4018 HudElement43Flag, 0x401C HudElement44Value, 0x4020 physics tick counter
vehicle_physics_01 PackedInputPacketFormat: packet+59 bit 1 -> byte this+0x4024
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased. The two 'this' interpretations (post-update resets vs HUD element flags) and the packet-byte write to 0x4024 cannot both be right on the same object unless the fields serve dual roles. This reinforces the possibility of distinct object bases between sources; resolved by keeping the sources' field identities per their own proposals until live proof disambiguates.

conflicts.subject: vehicle+0x3510/+0x3514 written both as vehicle mass / mass-with-payload and as wheel-block header anti-roll mixing factors
alternatives: mass fields (session a3+64 source)
anti-roll mixing factors in the wheel-block header
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased (source 02a unresolved). Not reconciled by this packet; kept in conflicts for the cross-reconciliation step.

conflicts.subject: vehicle+0xCC8 and +0xD0C described both as tracked-point flags and as front/rear wing transform presence flags
alternatives: tracked-point flags
front/rear wing transform presence flags
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased (source 02a unresolved). Dual role unresolved; kept in conflicts.

conflicts.subject: Wheel-dynamics record stride families are not provably the same array
alternatives: 62-dword (248-byte) stride records at this+0x35A0/0x35AC/0x35B0 (VehiclePhysicsBody, Vehicle)
1124-byte strided wheel-struct blocks, wheel 0 at this+0x5D8 (0x0043E230)
74-float (296-byte) stride wheel-state block at this+0xD4 (VehiclePhysicsObject)
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased. The 0x0043E230 wheel-struct blocks and the 0xD4 74-float block are different strided families; only the 248-byte records are shared across VehiclePhysicsBody and Vehicle (which supports that partial merge).

conflicts.subject: this+0x9C is both PhysicsStateBuffer heapBufferPtr and SuspensionSetup spring_array_ptr
alternatives: a heap buffer pointer freed through 0x00587BCF (PhysicsStateBuffer)
the growing spring array pointer (SuspensionSetup, capacity 0x94 / count 0x98)
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased. 0x00435410 (SuspensionSetup) calls 0x004358F0 (PhysicsStateBuffer) and both touch this+0x9C, so the two proposals may describe the same object, but the packet does not merge them; kept separate per rule 7.

conflicts.subject: Tire-object init markers at this+0x30/+0x34
alternatives: VehicleTireModel: initMarkerPrimary=0x30=-2, initMarkerSecondary=0x34=3
TireModelData: handle_sentinel_7 at 0x30, handle_pair_zero_6 at 0x34 (0/-1 sentinel scheme)
conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not erased. The two proposals are separate objects with numerically overlapping offset spaces (0x30/0x34); no evidence proves identity, so both interpretations are preserved on their own families.

unresolved: Common ownership of the this objects across VehicleControlState members (VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate, SteeringGeometryUpdate) and VehiclePhysicsBody members is NOT proven by the packet; VehicleControlState is a GUESS grouping on overlapping offset ranges. VehiclePhysicsBody is stronger (both touch the mode fields this+0x32BC/0x32C8 and the stride-62 wheel-dynamics records at this+0x35A0).

The suspension strut element layout behind the 316-byte stride (strut-relative +24/+72/+112..+156/+268/+272) is accessed by raw offsets only and is not defined anywhere in the packet; strut-relative offsets are recorded as source:raw prose, not as field evidence refs.
